title: Merge k sorted linked lists
summary: k sorted trains pull into one yard; keep every train's front carriage at a desk and always send out the smallest next.
goal: Join every sorted train into one sorted train

examples.label: Three trains
examples.explanation: The smallest front carriage always leaves next.

examples.label: One empty train
examples.explanation: The only train has no carriages.

ladder.name: Collect every carriage and sort
ladder.idea: Put all N carriages in one list and sort it.

ladder.name: Merge trains one at a time
ladder.idea: Merge the first two trains with the zipper merge, then merge the result with the third, and so on.
ladder.insight: Every train is already sorted, so the two-train zipper merge applies. But early carriages get re-merged k times.

ladder.name: A desk of front carriages
ladder.idea: Put each train's front carriage in a min-heap. Repeatedly send out the smallest and replace it with the next carriage of its train.
ladder.insight: The next carriage overall is always one of the k front carriages. A heap finds the smallest of k in log k steps, so each carriage is handled once.

transfer.problem: Combine k sorted log files from different servers into one log sorted by time.
transfer.explanation: Keep the next entry from each file in a min-heap and always output the earliest, refilling from the same file.

selfCheck: Puts only front carriages in the heap.
Pushes the next carriage of the train that just left.
Breaks ties between equal values without comparing nodes.
Handles empty trains and no trains.
